name: vrpn
why: A peripheral network protocol for VR trackers and devices; a niche door into hardware plumbing worth a look.

brief.what_it_is: VRPN (Virtual Reality Peripheral Network) is a library and set of servers that expose VR hardware, such as trackers, button boxes, dials, haptic devices, analog inputs, sound and imagers, over a network. A host PC at each VR station drives the peripherals, and the application talks to them through VRPN client classes without needing to know the network topology. The wiki describes a class-of-service abstraction in which all devices of one base type, such as trackers, produce the same kind of reports. The brew entry lists a vrpn_server executable, but I did not see that name in the pages I read.
brief.why_it_exists: The wiki frames it as a network-transparent interface between application programs and the physical devices used in a VR system, so the application stays unaware of where the hardware is attached. It was originally developed at the UNC CISMM NIH National Research Resource and has been maintained by Sensics and later ReliaSolve.
brief.how_it_works: Each device type has one or more servers that read the hardware, plus a client-side class that reads values from the device and controls its operation. The system types are Analog, Button, Dial, ForceDevice, Imager, Sound, Text and Tracker, and each abstracts a set of semantics for its device type. Applications can derive specialized classes for features of a particular device, such as setting a tracker's update rate; other trackers simply ignore commands they do not understand.
brief.install_notes: The repository README is short and points to two other files, README.Compile for compiling at other sites and README.Legal for legal information on offsite use. I could not retrieve either: both URLs I tried returned HTTP 404. The wiki says source downloads with submodules updated are on the GitHub releases page. Tested platforms per the wiki are Win32, Cygwin, Linux, macOS (32- and 64-bit), ARM Linux and Android. The wiki also notes a community tutorial by Daniel Wilches for compiling the client side on iPhone. I saw no information about Homebrew-specific steps, runtimes or first-run configuration.
brief.standout: It predates most modern VR middleware, and its core idea is a common device-class abstraction, so one tracker class covers many different tracker models. It is a plumbing layer that sits between VR apps and hardware, which is rarely visible to users.
brief.status: Maintained, with some doubt. The wiki's Home page was last edited June 23, 2019 across 25 revisions. The README says the project is 'currently maintained and supported by ReliaSolve in collaboration with a productive community of contributors.' The wiki also says some platforms are 'not actively maintained' and that the debian packaging branch is 'only good for 07.22 right now, due to lack of attention.' I did not find a release date or latest commit.
brief.caveats: Several platforms, including SGI/Irix, HP-UX, Solaris and older handheld Linux, are no longer actively maintained. The wiki's debian branch is described as lacking attention. The repository README defers compile and legal details to other files I could not reach. I did not see the licence, and the legal file is flagged as important for offsite use. The brew caveats field is empty.
quotes: The Virtual-Reality Peripheral Network (VRPN) is a set of classes within a library and a set of servers that are designed to implement a network-transparent interface between application programs and the set of physical devices (tracker, etc.) used in a virtual-reality (VR) system.
The application remains unaware of the network topology.
VRPN also provides an abstraction layer that makes all devices of the same base class look the same; for example, all tracking devices look like they are of the type vrpn_Tracker.

https://github.com/vrpn/vrpn: worked, returned a short repository README that points to README.Compile and README.Legal and to the Gitter chat
